newsitem.title: UK: UK pensions office launches new pensions enquiry.
newsitem.headline: UK pensions office launches new pensions enquiry.

text.p: The U.K. Office of Fair Trading (OFT) has launched an inquiry into the pensions industry to investigate consumers' experiences in buying pensions and the effect of their choice on pension entitlement.

"At a time when consumers are having to become more proactive in how they provide for their retirement, there is increasing unease about pensions products and selling methods employed by the industry," OFT Director General John Bridgeman said.
"People are now more worried about living too long to provide a comfortable retirement than they are about dying early."
The OFT announcement came just as a court told Kevin Maxwell, son of disappeared tycoon Robert Maxwell, that he would not have to face a second serious fraud trial.
The decision draws a line under five years of controversy surrounding some 400 million stg which disappeared from Maxwell company pension funds.
In January Kevin, his brother Ian and former Maxwell director Larry Trachtenberg were acquitted of conspiring to defraud the pension funds.
The 1995 Pensions Act, drafted largely as a result of the Maxwell affair, is due to come into effect in April 1997.

The final report from the OFT inquiry, scheduled for publication in the first half of 1997, will cover an analysis of actual or potential "detriment" to consumers in general and particular groups such as women who have taken career breaks.
It will also seek how such losses can be addressed and avoided in the future and make any necessary recommendations to ministers, regulatory bodies, the industry and consumers.
A further aspect will be a comparison with other pensions industries internationally.

Bridgeman said an important source of information will be responses gathered from consumers who have had both favourable and unfavourable experiences with the sale and performance of pension products.

This will be used in the final report but OFT will not be able to take up any individual case or complaint. Views will also be sought from the industry, regulators, consumer groups and other government and self regulatory organisations.
